global_issues.title: Hormuz tensions escalate, oil prices climb on Trump comments
global_issues.note: Confirmed. WTI and Brent both surged (~5%+) amid stalled US-Iran talks; Iran demands US lift naval blockade before reopening Hormuz. Trump's hardline posture (threats of intensified strikes) is consistent with recent reporting. No de-escalation in the last 24h.

global_issues.title: US 30-year yields hit highest since 2007 on oil and war fears
global_issues.note: Confirmed by multiple sources (Bloomberg, CNBC, Yahoo Finance). 30-year yield hit ~5.31%, a fresh 19-year high on Aug 18. Driven by combination of oil/war fears, heavy long-dated bond supply, persistent inflation, and AI-related hyperscaler borrowing — briefing's framing is directionally correct though slightly understates the fiscal/AI-borrowing drivers alongside war fears.

market_mood_check.note: Yellow/cautious framing matches reality: S&P 500 fell for a third consecutive session (-0.69%), Nasdaq -1.33%, semiconductor gauge -5.5%, all against a backdrop of 19-year-high 30-year yields and Hormuz-driven oil spike. MU's -7.02% headline figure is independently confirmed accurate (~$940.89 close, -7% day).

sector_check.note: Directionally correct that semiconductors (SMH) and growth/software lagged while yields rose, but the framing of CEG's resilience as tied to 'the oil move' is misleading — CEG is a nuclear/power utility whose strength is driven by AI-related electricity demand and its own Q2 earnings beat/raised guidance, not oil prices. The 'rotation to energy' framing overstates a broad energy-sector move; the real driver of chip weakness is more AI-capex-sustainability skepticism and heavy hedge-fund de-risking in the crowded semiconductor trade than yields alone.

grok_report.summary: The briefing's headline facts (Hormuz/oil spike, 30-year yields at a 2007 high, MU's -7.02% drop, TSM's ~$413 close) all check out against current reporting, and the yellow/cautious mood call is well-supported. The main gaps are contextual: it undersells the broader AI-capex-sustainability-driven semiconductor rout (Western Digital, SanDisk, Marvell, Seagate all down sharply) and omits Micron's company-specific Netlist patent litigation, while mischaracterizing CEG's resilience as an oil-driven 'energy sector' move rather than an AI-power-demand story.
